anomalies.obs: On the right tile, the LM1117-5.0 regulator U1 has both its input pin VI and its output pin VO wired to the same +5V power symbol (two +5V arrows directly above VI and VO). Meanwhile the VCC net – which carries the output decoupling cap C1, the TACH pull-up R6, the PMOS Q1 source and JP1 pin 2 – is not connected to U1's VO anywhere on the drawing; it is only reachable from +5V through the optional VCC_STABLE jumper JP1.
anomalies.exp: The LDO output (VO) should drive the regulated VCC rail, and its input (VI) should sit on the raw supply net, not on the same +5V net as the output. A 5 V LDO also needs input headroom above its 5 V output, so tying VI and VO together defeats regulation and leaves VCC undriven unless JP1 is closed.

evidence.quote: U1 LM1117-5.0: VI -> +5V, VO -> +5V (right tile, row A)
VCC net on root sheet connects C1, R6, Q1 source and JP1 pin 2; no wire to U1.VO (left tile, rows A-B)

anomalies.impact: The regulated VCC rail is not produced by the LDO; the regulator is wired input-to-output with zero dropout headroom. VCC (fan PMOS source and tachometer pull-up) is only powered if the VCC_STABLE jumper is closed to raw +5V, otherwise the fan-driver side is unpowered and the tach pull-up has no rail.

parsed.summary: The drawing shows the LM1117-5.0 (U1) with both VI and VO tied to the +5V net while the VCC rail that the fan driver and tach pull-up depend on is not connected to the regulator output, so the LDO is effectively shorted input-to-output and VCC is left undriven except through the optional jumper – a connectivity deviation from a normal regulated-rail design.
